title: kiki the nano bot
tagline: Steer a little robot through cubic nano worlds where down is wherever your wheels are.
summary: kiki is a small robot in a cube-shaped world. He drives forward and backward, turns, jumps, pushes stones, shoots and climbs: when he drives over an edge he rolls around it, and when he meets a wall he drives up it. Down is always under his wheels, so stones he pushes fall towards whatever is his floor.

Fifty levels lead from the first steps to wire stones that carry current from generators to motors, gears that drive each other, bombs that push everything around them, switches that open the exit and, at the end, a cube full of mutant bots. Every level counts your moves against the par of the original; the level list opens two new levels for each one you solve.

This is a port of kiki 1.0.2 (2006) by Thorsten Kohnhorst from its C++ and Python source: the same movement and timing, the same fifty levels, colour schemes, menus, 3D font and texts. Its sound effects are new (the original's sounds have no known licence).
caveat: Honest note: the game logic is checked against the original's own C++ code, built headless, and the levels against the original's level scripts; the drawing (three.js in place of OpenGL 1) follows the original's display code but has not been compared with the running original. The sound effects are not the original's: they are new ones, made for this port, because the licence of the original sounds is unknown.
